ok, and -ngl 0 means CPU only, right?
Yes. The Deck has no working CUDA or Vulkan path for llama.cpp here, so -ngl 0 keeps every layer on the CPU.

What batch size should I set? The model is small, but the texts are long.
For long texts keep -ub 512 and -c 2048. A batch of 2048 on the Deck CPU gives no gain and just eats memory.

chats.title: llama-server returns 503 on long context

messages.content: llama-server on 8080 returns 503 with long context. What's going on?

messages.name: bash
messages.content:
slot 0 | update_slots: failed to find free space in the KV cache
error: KV_CACHE_FULL_4417: no free cells, n_ctx=4096 requested=4410
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable  POST /v1/chat/completions
slot 0 | release: stop, 0 tokens generated
slot 1 | processing task 88
slot 1 | prompt eval time = 611.02 ms / 96 tokens
The error KV_CACHE_FULL_4417 means the cache is full: a request of 4410 tokens does not fit into n_ctx=4096. Increase -c to 8192 or reduce --parallel.
Won't --parallel 1 break other requests?
They will queue up, but the 503 errors will go away. For a single user that's fine.

The file is cp1251, the separator is ';', lines end with CRLF. So read it with encoding='windows-1251' and delimiter=';', and parse amounts with commas using decimal=','.
How do I make the parser detect the encoding on its own?
You can use chardet, but for a single bank it's simpler to specify the encoding and separator explicitly. That way the parser doesn't trip over empty lines.

chats.title: Borscht recipe for six servings

messages.content: How do I make borscht for 6 servings? Look for a recipe based on meat broth.

messages.name: bash
messages.content:
1. Classic beef borscht — Home Kitchen
   Pour cold water over 1.2 kg of beef, bring to a boil and skim off the foam. Simmer the broth on low heat until the meat is tender, then strain it and return it to the pot.
   Ingredients: bone-in beef, 2 beets, 300 g cabbage, 4 potatoes, carrot, onion, 2 tbsp tomato paste, vinegar, garlic, herbs.

2. Borscht on meat broth, step by step — Cooking Journal
   The key point is to stew the beets separately with vinegar so they keep their color. The zazharka is added 10 minutes before the end.
   Total time is about 2.5 hours, most of it spent on the broth.

3. Hearty borscht for a big group — Everyday Recipes
   Cook the beef 47 minutes after boiling, then add the potatoes and cabbage. Fry the beets and carrot with tomato separately and add them to the pot 15 minutes before it's done.
   For 6 servings, take 1.2 kg of meat and 3 L of water, salt at the end.

4. Lenten mushroom borscht — Home Deli
   Meatless version: mushroom broth from dried porcini, zazharka in sunflower oil, sour cream when serving.
   Yield about 2 liters, enough for 4 servings in normal portions.
5. Borscht with smoked ribs — Tasty and Simple
   Boil the ribs separately and make the broth from them with some meat added. Sour cream and garlic when serving.
   Good for a big family, cooking takes about 3 hours.

6. Diet borscht on chicken broth — Healthy Eating
   Chicken instead of beef, sauté the vegetables in minimal oil. Cooking time 1 hour 20 minutes.
   Yield about 3 liters, suitable for those watching calories.

According to the third recipe: cook the beef 47 minutes after boiling, then add the potatoes and cabbage. Fry the beets with tomato separately and add them 15 minutes before it's done. For 6 servings take 1.2 kg of meat and 3 L of water.
Ok, how much sour cream per serving?
About 200 g of sour cream is enough for 6 servings if you serve a big spoonful each.

chats.title: Sourdough hydration and bulk fermentation timing

messages.content: My sourdough is dense. How long should bulk fermentation run at 24C?

messages.name: bash
messages.content:
# bake log, November

## Bake 9 (Nov 8)
- flour: 500 g bread flour (T65)
- water: 390 g (78%)
- starter: 100 g, 4 days old, fed 1:1:1
- salt: 10 g
- bulk ferment 5h20m at 24C
- fold every 30 min x4
- shaping: batard, cold retard 12 h
- result: open crumb, slight gum line on the bottom

- flour: 500 g (T65)
- water: 370 g (74%)
- starter: 80 g, 9 days old

- result: tight crumb, good oven spring

Your bake 9 used bulk ferment 5h20m at 24C with four folds, which looks right. Dense loaves usually mean the starter was too young or the dough was under-proofed. Bake 10 with a mature starter gave a better crumb.
Hmm, my starter was 4 days old when I made it.
Feed it twice daily for a week before baking. A starter that is only four days old is not strong enough to lift a 78% hydration dough.
